page.layout: One column of text on one printed page. Top: a running heading line "ET CAPITUM." (centred, capitals). Then a list of numbered questions 14–21 in italic. Then a heading "SECTIO DECIMA" and a second heading "CAPUT UNICUM" (centred). Then a numbered list 1–6 with a large initial S, and at the foot a catchword-like line "7. Cir." set at right and a signature "S" at left. No margin notes.

main_text.head: ET CAPITUM.
main_text.p: 14. Quid si de litteris cambii incidat quæ-stio?
15. Quid si de valore nummorum contentio?
16. Quid si credita sint 10. dolia vini Aurelianensis, Amsterodami solvenda?
17. Quid si pupillo dandus sit tutor?
20. In integrum restitutione petita, quale statutum spectandum?
21. Quid si mulier adversus dotem velit restitui?
main_text.head: SECTIO DECIMA
CAPUT UNICUM.
main_text.p: 1. SI statuta varient circa actionum terminos, quæ spectanda?
2. Si intentanda actiones personales, quale statutum spectandum?
3. Si debitor à pluribus creditoribus conveniendus, ubi concursus judicium sit formandus, si particulare.
4. Quid si judicium sit universale, puta in cessione bonorum, beneficio intentarii, &c.?
5. Quid si creditorum unus per hypothecam sibi prospexerit abunde?
6. Cujus loci servanda solemnia circa procedendi modum?

page.notes: The large initial S of item 1 is printed as a woodcut-style letter. The catchword "Cir." and the signature "S" at the foot are partly damaged by scan wear; the last line is faint. The page number is not printed. Some letters in the scan are worn (e.g. "s" forms rendered as s).
